title: Sonny and the Still Pond | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka discovers a perfectly still moonlit pond that mirrors every star in the sky, and watches a gentle platypus glide silently through the silver water. A magical bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The evening was very still.

Little Sonny the quokka padded softly through the bush, following a thin silver path between the gum trees.

She could hear something up ahead. Or perhaps she could not hear anything at all. That was the thing about tonight — it was the quietest quiet she had ever known.

Then she stepped out from the trees and stopped.

There it was.

A pond. Round and dark and perfectly, perfectly still. Like a mirror lying flat on the ground.

And in the pond — the stars.

Every single star in the sky was reflected there, shimmering softly. The moon too, round and pale and full, floating just below the surface.

Sunny sat down at the water's edge and looked and looked.

Two skies, she thought. One above. One below.

Then something moved.

Very slowly, without a sound, a dark shape glided beneath the water. It was a platypus — small and smooth, with a wide soft bill and tiny paddle feet. It moved through the reflected stars like a dream drifting through a dream.

Sunny held her breath.

The platypus did not hurry. It simply glided. In and out of the starlight. Slow and easy and calm.

Sunny watched until her eyes grew heavy.

The pond stayed perfectly still. The stars stayed perfectly bright.

She lay down softly in the grass at the water's edge, where the moonlight was warm and the air smelled of earth and water and night.

Above her, the real stars blinked their slow, steady blinks.

Below her, in the pond, the reflected stars did the same.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little platypus. Goodnight, little one.
